name: Pancha Pandava Temples — the Five Shrines of the Pandavas
theme: Five Vishnu Divya Desams near Chengannur on the Pamba, each held to have been consecrated by one of the five Pandava brothers
region: Kerala (Chengannur and Changanassery, along the Pamba)
description: Within a short drive of one another in the Pamba country of central Kerala stand five temples of Vishnu that tradition links to the five Pandava brothers of the Mahabharata. After the war, the story goes, the brothers came south on pilgrimage and each consecrated a shrine: Yudhishthira at Thrichittatt, Bhima at Thiruppuliyur, Arjuna at Aranmula, Nakula at Thiruvanvandoor and Sahadeva at Thrikkodithanam. All five are Divya Desams of Malai Nadu, praised by Nammalvar, and all keep the Kerala temple form of copper-roofed sanctums within walled courtyards. Pilgrims often visit them in a single day, and the Aranmula temple adds its famous snake-boat regatta and the Vallasadya feast to the round in the monsoon season.
